chunks: From him, from his father, from Abu Umayr, from Hisham and Hammad and Ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr and others, all of them said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
"There is no charity (sadaqah) and no manumission (itq) except that which is intended for the Face of Allah, Exalted and Glorious."

key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (meaning for His sake alone)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for charity and manumission to be valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the validity of charity (sadaqah) and manumission (itq) is contingent upon the intention being exclusively for the sake of Allah, excluding any worldly motives or ostentation. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) as the spiritual core that transforms physical acts into true worship, ensuring they are accepted by the Divine.
